set.body:
Problem:
ResultAttachment reads, decodes, binds, and validates a result envelope, but Sojourn then rereads and decodes the same file to move successful value bytes into its content-addressed store. The repeated path adds work and opens semantic drift between validation and storage.

Scope:
- Introduce a verified result payload returned by attachment on success, carrying the decoded value plus the exact validated encoded bytes or an equivalent immutable digest-bound representation.
- Let Sojourn store the verified payload directly without reopening or redecoding the envelope.
- Preserve typed non-success evidence and keep bounded reads and epoch/release/schema/output validation authoritative in one place.

Acceptance criteria:
- A successful attachment performs one bounded envelope read and one envelope decode.
- The success value handed to the store is immutably bound to the submission key, attempt id and epoch, job binding, operation, schema, worker release, and validated output manifest.
- Sojourn contains no second ResultEnvelopeCodec.decode or result-file reread on the success path.
- Mutation or replacement of the envelope after attachment cannot change the bytes stored as the successful result.
- Oversized, malformed, wrong-schema, wrong-release, wrong-operation, stale-epoch, missing-value, and invalid-output cases cannot produce a verified payload.
- All failure and indeterminate diagnostics survive the mapping into TaskOutcome; successful audit evidence remains accessible through the durable handle or documented evidence surface.
- An instrumented test source proves one read and one decode; digest tests prove the stored RemoteRef names exactly the validated bytes.
- Existing canonical envelope fixtures remain byte-identical.
- scala-slurm managed/result suites and Sojourn batch/TCK suites pass with no unbounded result read.
set.title: SCOMP.4: Attach and store one verified result payload
